newsitem.title: GREECE: NEW WAVE OF STRIKES TO HIT GREECE ON MONDAY.
newsitem.headline: NEW WAVE OF STRIKES TO HIT GREECE ON MONDAY.

text.p: Greece is faced with more labour protest as the strike by municipal personnel went into its fifth day on Friday and the Panhellenic Seamen's Federation (PNO) announced a 48-hour strike that will begin on Monday.
Farmer representatives have also threatened to repeat recent road blockades in the near future, according to the morning press.
This new wave of strikes will hit Greece for the second time, since both farmers and seamen were striking during the pre-Christmas period.
The farmers' blockade of national auto routes lasted 24 days. They were protesting for higher price supports, less expensive fuel and lower Value Added Tax (VAT) on their equipment.
The impact from the sanitation workers' strike was beginning to be felt as big piles of litter were visible in the Athens and Piraeus districts.
Their union's secretary general, Dimitris Roris, told Reuters: "Our main demand is the conversion of employees' temporary contracts to indefinite duration ones."
Other demands included a doubling of the lump sum payment given on retirement, which currently stands at 1.3 million drachmas. Municipal workers also demanded a lower retirement age.

The seamen's union said in a statement earlier this week that it wanted a solution to three major issues -- worsening unemployment, better pension and insurance plans and keeping the favourable tax treatment that was valid until 1994.
"We demand what we consider proper and dignified pensions," said John Halas, the general secretary of P.N.O.
"Dialogue with deputy finance minister George Drys has been fruitless," he added.
Meanwhile, on Friday the first Agricultural Policy Council met under Prime Minister Costas Simitis, with an aim to achieve the modernisation of the farming sector.
"This is the crowning moment of social dialogue," said Costas Simitis.

"The government is implementing with steadfastness and consistency a programme with a time framework up to the year 2000, aimed at creating a strong agricultural sector," Simitis said. --Margarita Sotiropoulou, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
